title: Andre Previn at 17: facility but no style yet
summary: Callender and Willard discuss Previn's first session and his classical background, saying he had not developed a jazz style.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Back to Andre Previn. Do you remember what tunes you did on Andre's first session with Irving Ashby...
I'm not sure. I think one of them could have been "Honeysuckle Rose." I saw a list here, but I don't know where I put it.
You were looking in a Jepsen under "Andre Previn," and it his first session that they list was later than the one that you did.

Yeah, the one they listed was later. But this one was in 1946, and I haven't found... I imagine I could call...I could get... Irving might have the names. We could put that on later. But we did his first record date.
I don't even remember what label it was.
How did the session come about?

Well, at that time Andre I would say had the qualities of a good musician, but he was a little immature. You know, at 17 you... He could play, he had the facility, but he really wasn't into Jazz. He played what he had heard other people play at that time. He hadn't developed his own style.
I heard him play Classical Music at that point. He was a guest on the Frank Sinatra radio show when he was 17. That's when I first heard. He was there because Frank knew his father at MGM.
His father was a conductor at MGM, wasn't he.
Mmm-hmm. And he heard about this amazing teenager who played Classical piano, and had him on the
radio. So then it wasn't too long after that you started hearing a lot more about him. Then he was playing Jazz later. But he wasn't playing Jazz then.
Not real Jazz, no. I would say he was amazing for 17 years old, but he hadn't developed a style. He just had all the facility.
